=== FINDING 1 (BLOCKING, reproduced) -- scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py counts a review record that names NO commit, because `head.startswith("")` is True ===

scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py:197 and :206, inside review_records():
    reviewed = str(record.get("reviewed_commit", ""))
    ...
    if not head.startswith(reviewed):
A missing or empty `reviewed_commit` becomes "", and every string starts with "". The freshness test is therefore skipped entirely for exactly the record that names nothing, and the record is counted toward REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS on the ARMED MERGE PATH.

REPRODUCTION (driving the PR's own FakeRepo harness from tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py against the real aq.readiness; probe kept out of the tree):
    A  control, correct record                 -> ready=True   (harness sane)
    B  `reviewed_commit` key REMOVED           -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    C  `reviewed_commit` = ""                  -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    D  `reviewed_commit` = "a" (1-char prefix) -> ready=True   <-- DEFECT
    E  `reviewed_commit` = a different sha     -> ready=False  (correctly blocked)
    F  `reviewed_commit` = null                -> ready=False  (str(None) = "None")
Cases B and C are the ones that matter: a record that reviewed nothing at all is indistinguishable, to the armed path, from one that reviewed this exact head.

THE GUARD IS NOT WHOLLY VACUOUS, AND I SAY SO. Deleting the startswith line entirely makes test_a_stale_review_record_does_not_satisfy_the_gate fail, so case E is genuinely covered. What is uncovered is the absent/empty case: no test in tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py constructs a record without `reviewed_commit`. `_good_review()` always supplies one.

MITIGATION I MEASURED, so this is not overstated: reviews/schema.json lists `reviewed_commit` in `required`, and scripts/lwb_lanes.py enforces that schema, so a record with no `reviewed_commit` fails lwb-lanes -- which runs as a step inside the required `test` job, and readiness() requires every required check green before it counts reviews at all. So this is a second line of defence with a hole in it, not a one-step path to a bad merge. It is still blocking in my judgement: this script exists to be the thing that decides, it holds a write-scoped token when armed, and the repository's own standard (tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py's docstrings) is that a check must fail when what it guards is broken.

SUGGESTED FIX, one line: reject an empty `reviewed_commit` outright and require a minimum length before the prefix compare, e.g.
    if len(reviewed) < 7 or not head.startswith(reviewed):
plus a test that removes the key.

The owner should look at this directly -- it is the kind of thing where a green-looking PR page hides the fact that nothing has been checked.

=== FINDING 4 (NON-BLOCKING, reproduced) -- the module docstring's central honesty claim is false for two of its own reads ===

scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py's docstring ends:
    "Exits 0 when it reached a decision ... and 1 only when it could NOT
     decide -- an unreachable API, an unreadable record. 'I could not check'
     never shares an exit code with 'I checked and found nothing'."
But `_contents_json` and `_list_dir` both call `_gh(..., allow_fail=True)`, which swallows ANY non-zero gh exit and returns "".

REPRODUCTION (monkeypatching subprocess so every /contents/ call returns exit 1 with "HTTP 500: Internal Server Error", all other reads untouched):
    _list_dir("reviews/29", ...)      -> []
    _contents_json("proof/29.json",...) -> None
    review_records(29, head)          -> (0, ['no review records under reviews/29/ at deadbeefdead'])
An API outage is reported in the words of a clean, negative finding, and the process exits EXIT_DECIDED (0). That is the exact shape the PR body says this repository has been burned by three times, and the docstring claims immunity from it.

WHY NON-BLOCKING: it fails CLOSED. An outage reads as "gate unsatisfied", which refuses to merge; it cannot produce a spurious enqueue. The defect is the claim, not the safety. Either narrow the docstring or let these two helpers distinguish 404 (genuinely absent) from every other failure (CouldNotCheck).

- Full suite at this head: 515 passed in 19.3s. One pre-existing DeprecationWarning at tests/test_lwb_check_proof_reexecute.py:248 ("invalid escape sequence '\l'"), not introduced by this PR.
- python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py -> "lwb-proof check passed (19 record(s))", EXIT=0.
- THE GATE CHANGE IS REAL AND ITS TEST IS NOT VACUOUS. I mutation-probed it: removing the single line `".claude/",` from SHARED_PREFIXES in scripts/lwb_lanes.py makes test_classify_cli_config_dirs_are_shared FAIL with `assert 'other' == 'shared'` (1 failed, 63 passed). Restored; tree clean.
- "allow_auto_merge is false": TRUE. GET /repos/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-BuildCraft -> .allow_auto_merge = false.
- "the ruleset requires NINE checks": TRUE, and I counted them rather than trusting the number. Reading every ruleset's required_status_checks rule gives exactly nine contexts: test on (ubuntu|windows|macos)-latest x (3.10|3.12), plus lwb-portable on (ubuntu|windows|macos)-latest.
- required_contexts() refuses to treat an empty required-checks list as "all checks passed" (raises CouldNotCheck). check_conclusions maps a null conclusion to "pending", so a queued check is not a passing one. Both are the right shape.

=== A FALSE ACCUSATION I NEARLY MADE, AND CAUGHT ===

Having read the ruleset's nine required contexts and seen that `lwb-lanes` is not among them, I was about to charge that this repository's entire independent-review gate does not gate merging at all -- that a PR could go green with every required check passing and no review record. That charge is WRONG. `lwb-lanes` is a STEP inside the `test` job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:198), and `test` is required on six matrix legs. A red lwb-lanes step turns the whole `test` job red. I checked the workflow file before writing the finding rather than after, and it dissolved. The same applies to lwb-check-state-claims (ci.yml:182), which is why Finding 2 is blocking.
